120→|---|---|---|---|
 121→| `ruled` | The Judge issued a ruling and every gate passed | Yes | `decided` |
 122→| `withheld` | A gate stopped the ruling: confidence below threshold, amount above the cap, or an unmeasured deviation on a route case | Yes — the candidate is recorded for a human reviewer, never delivered | `under_review` |
 123→| `human_review` | The category is outside the two the agents handle | No — routed away before any agent | `passed_to_support` |
 124→| `needs_info` | The advocates asked targeted follow-up questions in the first round, or a blank form answer produced a template question | No — the run stops before the Judge | `needs_info` |
 125→
 126→## Gates enforced in code
 127→
 128→Six gates stand between a filing and a ruling, and each is enforced in Python, not asked of
 129→the model in a prompt:
 130→
 131→| Gate | File | Condition as written in code |
 132→|---|---|---|
 133→| Confidence threshold | `app/agents/judge.py` | `ruling.confidence < confidence_threshold` — the threshold is 0.65, read from `app/config.json` |
 134→| ESC-4, the autonomous cap | `app/agents/judge.py` | A money ruling whose `recommended_amount_sgd` exceeds the cap is withheld; the cap is SGD 50 from `app/config.json` |
 135→| ESC-2, unmeasured deviation | `app/agents/judge.py` | On a route-deviation case, `pack.route.deviation_pct is null` withholds the ruling — a route ruling must name the deviation it rests on |
 136→| One-round follow-up limit | `app/pipeline.py` | `if questions and not dispute.follow_up_answers` — a dispute is asked at most once; with answers present the Judge always runs and fresh questions are recorded but not sent |
 137→| Out-of-scope routing | `app/pipeline.py` | `if not dispute.is_agent_handled` — anything outside route deviation and no-show charge goes to human review before any agent runs; an unrecognised category normalises to "other" in `app/dispute.py` |
 138→| Answer once | `app/server.py` | The answers route claims the run with an exclusive create (`O_CREAT \| O_EXCL`) before re-running it — a `needs_info` run can be answered exactly once and cannot produce two rulings |
 139→
 140→Why in code? Because a prompt is a request — a model can misread it, and there is no
 141→recourse when it does. Code is a guarantee: the branch either runs or it does not, and the
 142→event log shows which. ESC-4 in particular moves money, so it must not depend on the LLM
 143→having read its instructions carefully.
 144→
 145→## Observability
 146→
 147→Every run writes three things under `runs/<run_id>/`:
 148→
 149→- `events.jsonl` — one JSON line per event, append-only, never rewritten: who sent what to
 150→  whom, when, with a one-line summary.
 151→- `payloads/` — the full payload behind each event, named by sequence number and event
 152→  type, so the strip stays readable and the detail stays one click away.
 153→- `case_file.json` — the assembled record: what was claimed, the evidence pack, both
 154→  advocate cases, the resolution, and the event strip. Self-contained, so one file tells
 155→  the whole story of one run.
 156→
 157→A run filed through the server writes one more file: `dispute.json`, the record the pipeline
 158→actually ran on (the command-line runner does not write it). When a `needs_info` run is
 159→answered, its directory also gains `answered.json`, recording which run the answers
 160→produced.
 161→
 162→The operator console (`ui/app.js`) renders the case file: the event strip shows one row per
 163→event — sequence, time, sender to recipient, summary — and expanding a row opens the full
 164→payload from the run directory attached in the browser. Payload references are sanitised, so
 165→a console loaded with a hostile file can be pointed at nothing outside the run. The
 166→command-line runner prints the same strip to the terminal.
 167→
 168→## What the parties see
 169→
 170→`party_view` in `app/server.py` is an allowlist that fails closed. The party page is handed
 171→exactly five keys — run id, dispute id, status, message, questions — and any malformed case
 172→file degrades to the neutral under-review message with no questions. A withheld ruling's
 173→amount and the Judge's confidence are structurally absent from everything the party is
 174→sent, not merely unrendered. `party_message_for_ruling` in `app/schemas.py` composes the
 175→decision message in code from structured fields — the action, the amount, and the plain
 176→titles of the policy rules cited — and the Judge's explanation never crosses this boundary:
 177→it stays in the operator console. Every non-decision status shows a canonical constant
 178→message, whatever a stale or planted case file might say. The two kinds of party-facing text
 179→are protected differently. The decision message is composed in code from structured fields,
 180→so nothing model-written reaches it: it names the action and the amount — a no-action ruling
 181→carries no amount — and at most three rule titles, never the escalation (ESC) rules.
 182→Follow-up questions, by contrast, are written by the advocates' model; the word check
 183→(`is_party_safe`, applied in `_questions_for_party` in `app/pipeline.py` and again in
 184→`party_view`) is what stops an unsafe one, and when no safe question survives, the pipeline
 185→falls back to plain template questions built from the form's own labels. The word list is
 186→incomplete, so for questions it is a real but imperfect filter. A run that asked for more
 187→information is answered through `POST /api/disputes/<run_id>/answers`, and the answers start
 188→a fresh run on the same dispute.
 189→
 190→## Policy and dataset packs
 191→
 192→`docs/policy.md` is data, not code: rules with IDs (GEN, EV, RD, NS, ESC families),
 193→preconditions written against pack fields in plain language, and per-rule provenance
 194→stating whether a rule comes from Ryde's own published policy, a comparable operator, or
 195→the project team. The pipeline reads it at the path in `app/config.json`; a different
 196→policy document drops in with no code change. Nothing in the code evaluates the
 197→preconditions — the Judge reads the rules and applies them in its reasoning. Citing a rule
 198→that does not exist is recorded rather than blocked: an unknown ID is logged under the
 199→ruling's `validation.unknown_rule_ids` with a note and the ruling still issues, but only
 200→titles of rules the policy actually defines can reach the party message.
 201→
 202→Two dataset packs live under `data/packs/`: `organiser-style-v1` — the default in
 203→`app/config.json` — which holds the corpus in the organisers' record shape, including their
 204→own DISP-002 verbatim; and `ryde-synth-v1`, the same 17 cases in this project's own record
 205→shape. Swapping corpora is a directory copy, never a code change. Each pack carries a
 206→`ground-truth.json` of expected outcomes, kept out of what the agents see: the agents get
 207→the dispute record, the evidence pack and the policy — never the answer — so replayed-run
 208→consistency can be measured honestly.
 209→
 210→## LLM provider
 211→
 212→Agent logic never talks to a vendor SDK. Every agent builds a request and calls one seam:
 213→the `LLMClient` interface in `app/llm/`, a single `complete` method whose response carries
 214→the text plus provenance (provider, model, usage, finish reason). Two adapters implement
 215→it. The mock provider, `app/llm/mock.py`, returns deterministic contract-shaped responses,
 216→so the full pipeline runs with no API key and the same dispute always produces the same
 217→decisions and the same computed figures (the run id and the event timestamps differ from
 218→run to run). Its free-text fields — claim summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation —
 219→carry a `MOCK` prefix, so a mock run can never be mistaken for a real ruling; actions, rule
 220→IDs and evidence refs are not prefixed, and the party decision message, composed in code,
 221→carries none. The Tencent adapter, `app/llm/tencent.py`, implements the same
 222→interface over HTTP — and is honest about its status: the concrete service, endpoint, auth
 223→scheme and payload shape are not pinned yet, the configuration still carries placeholder
 224→values, and the adapter fails loudly rather than silently falling back to the mock. To be
 225→plain: the Tencent endpoint has not been called. Every run to date is a mock run, a
 226→plumbing demonstration rather than a model judgement.
 227→
 228→## Limits
 229→
 230→What the system does not do yet, stated plainly:
 231→
 232→- **No real LLM calls.** The mock provider answers every agent. Nothing here has reasoned
 233→  about a dispute; the machinery around the reasoning is what is built and tested.
 234→- **Two categories only.** Route deviation and no-show charge. Property damage and safety
 235→

All three commits landed, working tree clean, final suite **345 tests, OK**.

- `f52c378` diagram (items 1–4) — withheld → human review edge "Candidate ruling queued"; dataset pack → server (and declared first); command-line runner node fed by the pack, feeding the category check; event log → console edge "Embedded in the case file" plus the corrected `## Diagram` sentence. Suite after: 345, 3 failures (prose pins).
- `f8e8a4a` doc prose (items 7–18) — numbers (pack + party's claim), raw questions in `advocate.follow_up_requested` vs the later check, template questions for blank fields, `dispute.json`/`answered.json`/answers route, the sixth gate (answer once, `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`), prose preconditions + Limits bullet, unknown rule IDs recorded not blocked, precise mock marking, same decisions not same file, decision-message details, word check as the real-but-imperfect question gate. Suite after: 345, 2 failures (README pins).
- `60359cc` README prose (items 5–6) — three gates naming ESC-2 with the RD-0108 example (verified by running it: withheld, no deviation to measure); advocate rows now "Builds the rider's/driver's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy". Suite: 345, OK.

The Mermaid block is byte-identical in both files (pinned by `test_one_mermaid_diagram_shared_with_the_readme`).

**Found while reading:** `README.md` still says "Every mock string is prefixed `MOCK`" — the same imprecision item 16 corrects in the doc, but the brief scoped item 16 to the Components row and `## LLM provider`, so I left the README caveat untouched and flag it here. The mock prefixes its free-text fields only; actions, rule IDs and evidence refs are unprefixed.
